newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to verify all mineral discoveries.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to verify all mineral discoveries.

text.p: All non-oil and gas mining companies operating in Indonesia will be required to have their discoveries verified by the government before they are made public, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.

The mines and energy ministry's new secretary-general, Darmoko Slamet, was quoted as saying the requirement would be included in new mining regulations to be issued soon and aimed at preventing the recurrence of scandals such as the Busang debacle.

"We will require all mining companies to report all their activities, including any finds," he was quoted as saying. He said the companies would also be required to submit quarterly reports to the government.
He said the future of the companies' contracts would depend on a government assessment of reports submitted during the first year of operations.

Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd estimated that the Busang property contained some 71 million ounces of gold, making it the century's biggest find. A later independent test showed it was almost worthless.
Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd found that data pegged to Busang was falsified on an unprecedented scale, making it the biggest mining fraud in history.
Indonesian authorities and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the scandal. Bre-X meanwhile has been delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSE).
Slamet said Bre-X had taken advantage of Indonesian mining rules by announcing the Busang discovery on the TSE, sending its share price soaring.
But he said the government had confidence in other mining companies operating in Indonesia. "There are still many good bona fide foreign mining companies," he said.

Slamet said foreign mining companies played an important role in the development of the country's mineral resources as local firms were not yet fully capable of or interested in tapping into the high-risk sector.
Slamet was appointed on Monday by Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana, replacing Umar Said, who had handled the Indonesian side of the Bre-X case in recent months.
Sudjana said his replacement was a routine move and had nothing to do with the Busang scandal.
